match_note: Round 1 (Version 0) has reports from R1, R2 (an early-career co-reviewer of another report, no comments of their own), R3 and R4. Version 2 has R4 again and a new referee R5; Version 3 has R5 only. The first-round manuscript matches v1: R1 quotes the page-3 sentence 'it lies in the correct energy range for intra-band excitations ... [22]' verbatim and cites Fig. S3; R3 and R4 cite Figs. 3a-3d, 4c and S2 with the same content as v1. The polarization-dependent data (Fig. S5) and acoustic-plasmon analysis were added in revision.

concerns.quote: Could the authors specify more precisely which results from Ref. [22] are being referenced here, and how the corresponding energy value is obtained?
concerns.summary: The statement that the low-energy feature lies in the energy range of intraband excitations per Ref. [22] does not say which calculated quantity or value is meant.

concerns.quote: the reshaping of the Fermi surface in the tight-binding picture and the band crossing at -2 eV not falling precisely on the H point anymore as it is the case in the DFT calculation?
concerns.summary: The tight-binding bands in Fig. S3 deviate from DFT in the ALHA plane, with the -2 eV crossing displaced from H.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the ability of RIXS to detect particle hole excitation has been well-established
concerns.summary: RIXS detection of particle-hole excitations is established and MgB2 is described by a band picture without correlations, so the work offers few new insights and suits a specialized journal.

concerns.quote: Is there Ei dependence of the RIXS spectrum?
concerns.summary: The incident-energy dependence of the RIXS spectrum is not shown.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The suppression of intensity going towards the M point in Fig 3b was attributed to a polarization effect- is there complementary XAS data to support this?
concerns.summary: The attribution of intensity suppression towards M to a polarization effect lacks supporting data.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Why is the lineshape of the quasiparticle continuum as measured with RIXS different than the lineshape predicted by the simulations and calculations?
concerns.summary: The measured continuum has a high-energy tail absent from the more symmetric simulated lineshapes, and a direct lineshape comparison on the Fig. 3a cuts is not shown.

concerns.quote: What is the branch in Fig 3d centered at ~1eV? Is it pi-pi intraband excitations? Was its absence a polarization effect?
concerns.summary: A calculated branch near 1 eV in the Lindhard function is not identified, nor is its absence from the data explained.

concerns.quote: What is the peak at 3eV in Fig S2? Is it plasmon- predicted to be at 3eV in section E of the Supplemental Materials. Why is it so broad?
concerns.summary: The origin and large width of the 3 eV peak are not explained.

concerns.quote: What is so special about the band structure of MgB2 for the Lindhard continuum to be separately observed from the rest of the particle hole excitation
concerns.summary: The paper does not explain why MgB2 was chosen or what lets its Lindhard continuum separate from other particle-hole excitations.

concerns.quote: While I agree that this is the case in a high-density metal, it would be good to state this nuance. In low-density- or semi-metals, this is not necessarily true.
concerns.summary: The claim that EELS cannot see the continuum holds only for high-density metals and should also be stated for non-resonant IXS.

concerns.quote: Along which direction is q in Fig. 3a? Is there a significant difference between the data with q taken along Γ-M versus Γ-K?
concerns.summary: The momentum direction in Fig. 3a is not stated and the Γ-M versus Γ-K comparison is not shown.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Is the value of q⊥ taken into account in the simulations, e.g. in Fig. 3c?
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether out-of-plane momentum transfer is included in the simulations.

later_concerns.quote: I suggest that the authors indicate this shift more clearly in the figure, e.g. with a dashed vertical line.
later_concerns.summary: Mark the polarization-dependent peak shift in the new Fig. S5.

later_concerns.quote: There is no information about the scattering geometry of the polarization-dependent spectra shown in Fig. S5, apart from the angle of incidence.
later_concerns.summary: Scattering angle, proximity to Bragg reflections and momentum range of the new polarization data are not given.

later_concerns.quote: In MgB2, Gao et al. predict an AP energy of approximately 450 meV, which is comparable to the Lindhard excitation observed here
later_concerns.summary: An acoustic plasmon predicted near 450 meV in metal diborides could explain the feature and is not considered.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the noticeable increase in linewidth of the RIXS feature is not discussed in the manuscript and is not adequately captured by the Lindhard response model.
later_concerns.summary: Linear low-q dispersion and linewidth growing with q are what a damped acoustic plasmon would show, and the linewidth increase is not explained.
